The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be the smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable, boundaryless oriented and time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Its smooth real $k$-forms are sections of $\bigwedge^kT^*M$, written $\Omega^k(M)$, and $d$ is the exterior derivative of [[lem-emg-lorentz-hodge-calculus]]. A smooth two-form $F$ is **closed** when $dF=0$ and **exact** when $F=dA$ for some smooth real one-form $A$ on the whole base.

Let $M$ be a smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable oriented four-manifold, and let $(U_i,g_{ij},a_i;\kappa_0)$ be a normalized circle-connection datum as in [[def-emg-local-potentials-and-circle-data]]. Use the set-sized-object and quotient convention of [[def-emg-set-size-and-class-schema]]. Then the chart data construct a smooth Hausdorff second-countable right principal $U(1)$-bundle $\pi:P\to M$ and a global smooth real connection one-form $\omega$ on $P$. Its curvature is basic: there is a smooth closed two-form $f\in\Omega^2(M)$ with $d\omega=\pi^*f$ and $f|_{U_i}=da_i$. The local potentials $A_i=\kappa_0a_i$ satisfy $dA_i=F$, where $F=\kappa_0 f$ is global. For two connections on the same fixed bundle with the same transition functions, their local-form differences are restrictions of one global base one-form; adding a global one-form to all local representatives stays in that bundle sector.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $P\to M$ be a smooth right principal
$G$-bundle with a principal connection $H$, and let
$\Phi\in\mathcal G(P)$. Then
$$\Phi_*H:=d\Phi(H)$$
is a principal connection. If $K_H$ and $K_{\Phi_*H}$ are the vertical-valued
curvatures from
[[def-principal-connection-and-vertical-curvature]], then for
$X,Y\in T_pP$,
$$K_{\Phi_*H}(d\Phi_pX,d\Phi_pY)=d\Phi_p(K_H(X,Y)).$$
Composition makes this a left action of $\mathcal G(P)$ on the set of
principal connections.
For every smooth map $F:M\to N$ and every form $\omega$ on $N$, $$d(F^*\omega)=F^*(d\omega).$$

Let $M^n$ be an oriented smooth manifold without boundary. For each compact set $K\subseteq M$ there are finitely many nonnegative smooth functions $\chi_i$ with compact supports contained in connected coordinate domains $U_i$, such that $\sum_i\chi_i=1$ on a neighbourhood of $K$. For $\omega\in\Omega_c^n(M)$ define
$$\mathcal I_M(\omega)=\sum_i I_{\phi_i}(\chi_i\omega)\quad(K=\operatorname{supp}\omega),$$
using the signed chart integrals. This value is independent of the finite functions and charts. It defines a linear functional, is local under restriction to an open set containing the support, and for $n\ge1$ satisfies
$$\mathcal I_M(d\eta)=0\qquad(\eta\in\Omega_c^{n-1}(M)).$$
For $n=0$ it is the finite signed sum $\sum_{p\in\operatorname{supp}\omega}\varepsilon(p)\omega(p)$. All assertions are choice-free: no partition on the entire manifold is required.

derivations.claim: On each overlap $U_i\cap U_j$, compatibility gives $\alpha_j=a_j'-a_j=(a_i'+\lambda(g_{ij}))-(a_i+\lambda(g_{ij}))=\alpha_i$. The forms therefore agree on overlaps and define one global smooth real one-form $\alpha$; uniqueness follows because the $U_i$ cover $M$. No global phase lift of any transition function is chosen.

Conversely, if $\alpha\in\Omega^1(M)$ is any smooth global real one-form, then $(a_i+\alpha|_{U_i})_i$ obeys $(a_j+\alpha|_{U_j})=(a_i+\alpha|_{U_i})+\lambda(g_{ij})$ because the restrictions of $\alpha$ agree on overlaps. Thus translation by $\alpha$ stays in the same bundle sector, and the set of representatives is affine over $\Omega^1(M)$.

By the curvature definitions in [F2], on every $U_i$ we have $f'-f=da_i'-da_i=d(a_i'-a_i)=d\alpha|_{U_i}$. Both sides are global, so the local equalities give $f'-f=d\alpha$ on $M$. Multiplying by the same constant $\kappa_0$ gives $F'-F=\kappa_0d\alpha$.

For a compact oriented smooth surface $S$ without boundary, pullback commutes with $d$ by [F4], so $\iota^*(F'-F)=\kappa_0d(\iota^*\alpha)$. The one-form $\iota^*\alpha$ has compact support because $S$ is compact; [F5] therefore gives $\int_S\iota^*(F'-F)=\kappa_0\int_Sd(\iota^*\alpha)=0$. Hence the physical curvature integrals agree.

On a trivializing chart, let $\Phi_h(x,z)=(x,h(x)z)$. Its inverse sends $(x,z)$ to $(x,h(x)^{-1}z)$. The connection form for the pushed-forward horizontal distribution is $(\Phi_h^{-1})^*\omega$, because its kernel is $d\Phi_h(\ker\omega)$. With $\omega=\eta+a_i$ from [F2] and $\eta=-iz^{-1}dz$, the product rule [F6] gives $(\Phi_h^{-1})^*\eta=\eta-\lambda(h)$ and hence $a_i'=a_i-\lambda(h)$. This is the pushforward sign; a pullback action by $\Phi_h$ instead has the opposite sign.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Let $g_\epsilon=g+\epsilon h+O(\epsilon^2)$ be a smooth variation of an oriented Lorentzian metric on a four-manifold, and let $\omega_\epsilon=\omega+\epsilon\tau+O(\epsilon^2)$ be a smooth variation of a $k$-form, $0\le k\le4$. Define $h_a{}^b:=g^{bc}h_{ac}$, $\operatorname{tr}_g h:=g^{ab}h_{ab}$, and
$$\bigl(h^\sharp\!\cdot\omega\bigr)_{a_1\ldots a_k}:=\sum_{j=1}^k h_{a_j}{}^b\omega_{a_1\ldots a_{j-1}b a_{j+1}\ldots a_k},$$
with $h^\sharp\!\cdot\omega:=0$ for $k=0$. Then
$$\left.\frac{d}{d\epsilon}\right|_0\star_{g_\epsilon}\omega_\epsilon=\star_g\left(\tau+\frac12(\operatorname{tr}_g h)\omega-h^\sharp\!\cdot\omega\right).$$
In particular, for the geometric background $\mathcal F$ and perturbation $f$ of [[def-emg-fx-linearized-electrovac]],
$$\delta(\star\mathcal F)=\star_g\left(f+\frac12(\operatorname{tr}_g h)\mathcal F-h^\sharp\!\cdot\mathcal F\right).$$
If $(h,f)$ satisfies the linearized Maxwell equation, then $d\,\delta(\star\mathcal F)=0$; this last condition is exactly the derivative of $d(\star_{g_\epsilon}\mathcal F_\epsilon)=0$, not a consequence of the variation formula alone.

citations.quote:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as inherited from the smooth principal-connection convention. Fix an oriented, time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N,o)$ and a fixed normalized $U(1)$ connection sector as in the fixed-topology affine-sector result. Its connection variations are global smooth real one-forms $\alpha,\beta\in\Omega^1(M)$, with components of unit $\mathrm m^{-1}$ in length-coordinate charts. Length-coordinate charts use metre-valued coordinates, with $x^0=ct_{\mathrm{sec}}$ when time is recorded in seconds; $c$ is a coordinate unit-conversion scale in $\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$, with no numerical measured value or physical role asserted. Impose the fixed-background Maxwell operator equations $d\star_g d\alpha=0$ and $d\star_g d\beta=0$, where $\star_g$ is the oriented Lorentzian Hodge map of signature $(-,+,+,+)$. Define the real three-form

$$\omega_g(\alpha,\beta):=\alpha\wedge\star_g d\beta-\beta\wedge\star_g d\alpha.$$

Let $\iota_\Sigma:\Sigma\hookrightarrow M$ be an oriented smooth embedding of a possibly noncompact three-dimensional manifold, and require the induced metric $\gamma:=\iota_\Sigma^*g$ to be positive definite. Its oriented Riemannian volume form is the nowhere-vanishing three-form $\mathrm{vol}_\gamma$ whose expression in each positively oriented chart $y=(y^1,y^2,y^3)$ is $\sqrt{\det(\gamma_{ij})}\,dy^1\wedge dy^2\wedge dy^3$. Let $\mu_\gamma$ be the positive smooth density measure with coordinate expression $d\mu_\gamma=\sqrt{\det(\gamma_{ij})}\,d^3y$. The density-measure integration supplier listed below gives the chart-independent measure and integral; for a real $L^1(\mu_\gamma)$ function its signed integral is the finite difference of the integrals of its positive and negative parts, and its chart formula is absolutely convergent.

There is a unique smooth real function $u_{\alpha,\beta}$ on $\Sigma$ such that $\iota_\Sigma^*\omega_g(\alpha,\beta)=u_{\alpha,\beta}\,\mathrm{vol}_\gamma$. Define the pairing $\Omega_\Sigma(\alpha,\beta)$ precisely when $u_{\alpha,\beta}\in L^1(\Sigma,\mu_\gamma)$, meaning $\int_\Sigma|u_{\alpha,\beta}|\,d\mu_\gamma<\infty$, and then set $\Omega_\Sigma(\alpha,\beta):=\int_\Sigma u_{\alpha,\beta}\,d\mu_\gamma$. This absolute-integrability condition is the convergence convention on noncompact $\Sigma$ and makes the value independent of any exhaustion or ordering. In length coordinates on $\Sigma$, the coefficients of $d\alpha$ and $d\beta$ have units $\mathrm m^{-2}$, those of $\omega_g$ have units $\mathrm m^{-3}$, $u_{\alpha,\beta}$ has units $\mathrm m^{-3}$, and $d\mu_\gamma$ has volume units $\mathrm m^3$; thus the normalized integral is dimensionless. Replacing normalized variations by physical-potential variations $\kappa_0\alpha$ and $\kappa_0\beta$ multiplies the current by $\kappa_0^2$; an action prefactor is not fixed here.

This is a mathematical fixed-metric Maxwell-block definition. The equations are imposed on the normalized connection variations. The item does not identify $\kappa_0d\alpha$ with the geometric-normalized electrovac field of the coupled Einstein–Maxwell equations, prescribe a conversion between those normalizations, include metric variations, or claim to define the full coupled covariant phase-space current.

Let $M$ be a smooth manifold, possibly with boundary. For $k\ge1$, $c\in C_k^\infty(M;\mathbb R)$ and $\omega\in\Omega^{k-1}(M)$, define integration over a chain by the finite linear sum of its simplex integrals. Then
$$\int_c d\omega=\int_{\partial c}\omega.$$
The zero chain has integral zero. In degree zero the boundary is zero; no degree-minus-one form is required by this statement.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be an arbitrary measure space. Let $f_n:X\to[0,+\infty]$ be measurable for every $n\ge1$, with $0\le f_1\le f_2\le\cdots$, and suppose $f_n(x)\uparrow f(x)$ for every $x\in X$. Then
$$\int f_n\,d\mu\uparrow\int f\,d\mu.$$

derivations.claim: Applying the graded product rule to each term of [F1] gives $d\omega_g=d\alpha\wedge\star_g d\beta-\alpha\wedge d\star_g d\beta-d\beta\wedge\star_g d\alpha+\beta\wedge d\star_g d\alpha$. The first and third terms cancel because the two-form pairing in [F2] is symmetric, and the other two vanish by the stated equations. Hence $d\omega_g=0$.

Since $d^2\chi=0$ by [F2], the change in [F1] under $\alpha\mapsto\alpha+d\chi$ is exactly $d\chi\wedge\star_g d\beta$. On the other hand, $d(\chi\star_g d\beta)=d\chi\wedge\star_g d\beta+\chi\,d\star_g d\beta=d\chi\wedge\star_g d\beta$. The current change is therefore the exact three-form $d(\chi\star_g d\beta)$.

Integrating the exact change over a finite smooth singular three-chain $c$ and applying [F3] gives $\int_c d(\chi\star_g d\beta)=\int_{\partial c}\chi\star_g d\beta$. This is zero when $c$ is a cycle, while for a chain with boundary it is the displayed boundary flux.

Now let $\Sigma$ be noncompact, assume both current pairings in the Statement are defined, and choose a compact Borel exhaustion with finite-chain representatives as in the Statement. Define the real three-form

$$\omega_g(\alpha,\beta):=\alpha\wedge\star_g d\beta-\beta\wedge\star_g d\alpha.$$

Let $\iota_\Sigma:\Sigma\hookrightarrow M$ be an oriented smooth embedding of a possibly noncompact three-dimensional manifold, and require the induced metric $\gamma:=\iota_\Sigma^*g$ to be positive definite. Its oriented Riemannian volume form is the nowhere-vanishing three-form $\mathrm{vol}_\gamma$ whose expression in each positively oriented chart $y=(y^1,y^2,y^3)$ is $\sqrt{\det(\gamma_{ij})}\,dy^1\wedge dy^2\wedge dy^3$. Let $\mu_\gamma$ be the positive smooth density measure with coordinate expression $d\mu_\gamma=\sqrt{\det(\gamma_{ij})}\,d^3y$. The density-measure integration supplier listed below gives the chart-independent measure and integral; for a real $L^1(\mu_\gamma)$ function its signed integral is the finite difference of the integrals of its positive and negative parts, and its chart formula is absolutely convergent.

There is a unique smooth real function $u_{\alpha,\beta}$ on $\Sigma$ such that $\iota_\Sigma^*\omega_g(\alpha,\beta)=u_{\alpha,\beta}\,\mathrm{vol}_\gamma$. Define the pairing $\Omega_\Sigma(\alpha,\beta)$ precisely when $u_{\alpha,\beta}\in L^1(\Sigma,\mu_\gamma)$, meaning $\int_\Sigma|u_{\alpha,\beta}|\,d\mu_\gamma<\infty$, and then set $\Omega_\Sigma(\alpha,\beta):=\int_\Sigma u_{\alpha,\beta}\,d\mu_\gamma$. supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Let $\pi:P\to M$ be a smooth right principal $G$-bundle as in
[[def-smooth-principal-g-bundle]]. A **smooth gauge transformation** of $P$ is
a smooth diffeomorphism $\Phi:P\to P$ satisfying
$$\pi\circ\Phi=\pi,\qquad \Phi(pg)=\Phi(p)g\quad(p\in P,\ g\in G).$$
Here diffeomorphism has the meaning of
[[def-diffeomorphism-and-local-diffeomorphism-of-manifolds]]. The **gauge
group** $\mathcal G(P)$ is the set of these transformations under composition.
The identity is a smooth diffeomorphism and composites of smooth maps are
smooth by
[[prop-identity-maps-and-composites-of-smooth-maps-are-smooth]]; composites of
diffeomorphisms are diffeomorphisms because their inverses are composites of
the smooth inverses. The identity covers $M$ and commutes with the right
action. If $\Phi,\Psi\in\mathcal G(P)$, then $\Phi\circ\Psi$ covers $M$ and
$(\Phi\circ\Psi)(pg)=\Phi(\Psi(p)g)=\Phi(\Psi(p))g$, so the conditions are
closed under composition. The inverse of such a $\Phi$ also covers $M$: if
$q=\Phi(p)$ then $\pi(\Phi^{-1}(q))=\pi(p)=\pi(q)$. Equivariance gives
$$\Phi^{-1}(qg)=\Phi^{-1}(\Phi(p)g)=\Phi^{-1}(\Phi(pg))=pg.$$
Its smoothness is part of the diffeomorphism condition. Hence these maps form a
group under the composition law of [[def-group]].

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $P\to M$ be a smooth right principal
$G$-bundle with a principal connection $H$, and let
$\Phi\in\mathcal G(P)$. Then
$$\Phi_*H:=d\Phi(H)$$
is a principal connection. If $K_H$ and $K_{\Phi_*H}$ are the vertical-valued
curvatures from
[[def-principal-connection-and-vertical-curvature]], then for
$X,Y\in T_pP$,
$$K_{\Phi_*H}(d\Phi_pX,d\Phi_pY)=d\Phi_p(K_H(X,Y)).$$
Composition makes this a left action of $\mathcal G(P)$ on the set of
principal connections.
